meta.title: Leo's Bike Coat
meta.textType: story: teacher feedback and written instructions

paragraphs: Today Teacher Kim has a special lesson about bikes. She wants to teach the class about a safe ride. Leo comes to school in a big red coat. It is a hot day, and the coat is very silly. "Why do you wear a coat?" asks Lily. "It is my bike coat," says Leo. "I like it!" Teacher Kim holds up a blue helmet. Then she writes on the board: "Read and match."

The children look at a poster with six pictures and six words. Lily and Leo work together. Leo puts the word "helmet" with the picture of the helmet. "Well done, Leo!" says Teacher Kim. Then Leo puts the word "bike" with a picture of a shoe. Teacher Kim looks at the poster. "That is a mistake," she says. "Look again. Try again." Leo looks at the pictures. "Oh! The bike is here!" he says.

Now the word is in the right place. "Good work," says Teacher Kim. At break, Leo takes off his coat and puts on the helmet. "Do I look silly now?" he asks. "No," says Lily. "You look like a bike star." Before the bell, Teacher Kim writes the homework. "Ask Mom or Dad about a bike. Then write one sentence." Leo smiles. "I like my helmet," he says. "I like my coat too!"
